a.text: How absurd it is that we're chasing illusions on this battlefield full of bones, blood, smoke and mud.
The illusions are our only clue. Like the Lich said, the drifting fragments of history are the tracks it left behind.
We passed through many ruins, some long-forgotten, some never remembered to begin with.
Soon, these sights will be gone too. Many times we barely arrived in time to grasp the last traces.
We found seventeen Vampire War Arts Circles.
There are maybe dozens more... maybe even hundreds more of them on this battlefield.
They all appeared within the past week, a scary level of efficiency.
We found troop tracks on two of them, but the marks indicated that the troops were only on maintenance or patrol missions.
I doubt there's much point to destroying the Arts Circles. They could easily replace them with new ones.
It's only that much more important to take control of that thing, whatever it is.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: This place is completely ruined.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Just like the Rhodes Islanders said, it's another secret network of routes that lead into the city.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Through these hubs, Theresis has shipped huge amounts of steel, crystal units and witchcraft devices into Londinium, enough to repair The Shard and complete that airship.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But how did these materials reach Londinium? Even the dumbest dukes wouldn't let large shipments of materiel outside their control to travel freely around Victoria.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's probably that they, like the Nachzehrer King's legion, appeared out of thin air around the hubs.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The so-called Sarkaz supply line we've been looking for may be the last and least important step of the transport process.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: How did they do it?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Not only that, if Theresis had access methods like this, why isn't he using them directly in battle?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Teleporting armies behind enemy lines, or plopping Originium bombs right on top of ducal flagships.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Either there are limitations to the method... or it's actually really fragile.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The Lich called it an Art beyond the realm of Originium Arts, but I just couldn't picture it...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: W, over there—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Uh, no sign of battle. It's completely collapsed.

a.text: W has looked detached ever since that encounter a few days ago.
I saw her gaze absent-mindedly into the fire while on night watch.
I can't help her. She'll get through this on her own.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let's go. There's nothing to see here.

a.text: I look at the map in my hand. Scattered dots mark the locations of the Vampire Arts Circles.
I added a few, including the logistics hub just now, and the Nachzehrer King's legion camp.
Something had been placed there using the same methods.
There must be something linking them.
I scan the names on the map. Hills, valleys, small patches of forests, and a few small ponds.
Some sort of commonality? Shared geographical traits?
My eyes fall upon the name of a town. Brentwood.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ines, you said that Rhodes Island analyzed the intel from the Defense Forces command tower, where they had set their sights near a town by the name of Brentwood.

a.text: I draw a circle around Brentwood's location.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Closure came up with the analysis. She stole the records of all cargo movement since Theresis entered the city in 1094, and created an overlapping route map.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: All the towns around Londinium were covered in these cargo movements on the map.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's Victoria's capital, after all. All the steak and wine the citizens enjoyed before the war didn't grow on the shelves.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But the area around Brentwood is strangely empty, with only a few scattered entries around 1094 and 1095.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's pretty weird. Like there's a forgotten town right here in the middle of Victoria.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The Rhodes Islanders think Brentwood might be the starting point of the Sarkaz underground railroad, or the hub of a hidden network, implementing some sort of secret embargo.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We just proved the existence of these logistics hubs.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But, we also learned that Theresis has a pair of, well, invisible hands, which lets him puts things anywhere he wants.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We may need to reassess the significance of Brentwood.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The closer we get, the more Vampire Arts Circles we see.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Meanwhile, if we draw a line from the furthest points to Brentwood, we see that they're about equidistant. That might be the logistical limit.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Stop guessing. I know Brentwood. You couldn't hide anything in that poor-ass town. There were barely any Sarkaz vagrants when I visited a few months ago.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Maybe the caravans just don't pass through 'cause there's nothing interesting there.

a.text: W disinterestedly throws a rock over.
She's in a bad mood alright. She would normally have thrown a grenade pin.
The rock rolls on the map and falls right where I'm looking. I'm about to move it out away—
There's a patch of hills not far behind Brentwood. The rock fell right in the middle of the icons representing hills.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let's go. It's not like we have any better leads. Maybe coincidence has something in mind.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let's start there.

a.text: The hills are dark and eerie.
A Victorian history book wrote that the study of history is like walking into a cave, feeling the grains on the wall.
Working blindly in the dark, all you can do is try to piece together the puzzle of where we came from by feeling around in the darkness.
This land is not friendly to history.
Originium veins assimilate any organic tissue around them, even bones.
All that archaeologists had to work with are Originium-infested ruins. All they could do is mull over metal shards.
But we are different. We are Sarkaz.
We have many ways to look back. Legends say that the revenants in the furnace of Kazdel whisper the achievements of a certain King of Sarkaz, or the sad ending of another.
When I was little, I used to wait by the furnace that never went out, hoping to capture a single echo from the past.
But all I ever heard was silence.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You might actually be right. There's something unusual about the shadows here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: There seems to be a pattern in the chaos.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's like the ripples created by a sailing ship, overlapping and interfering with one another, until nothing is left but entropy.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Not so much sailing as... drifting.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Drifting.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I once heard a story from an old Diαblo, this word came up in his broken whispers.

steps.name: W
steps.text: What story?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: A story of disaster.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let's hope we don't run into the stuff of those stories.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let's hope we still have some good luck left in the bank.

steps.name: W
steps.text: A merc who thinks he's lucky is a dead merc.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Which is why we need you to stay behind, W.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We're not here to fight. We need to figure out what we're facing.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: If things go south and we need to pull out...

steps.name: W
steps.text: Don't worry, I won't leave the way open for you.

steps.name: W
steps.text: I'll set up the explosives and wait until you're almost at the exit, Vampires and Nachzehrer hot on your tail, maybe Theresis himself, and just as you're about to see the light...

steps.name: W
steps.text: Boom!

steps.name: W
steps.text: You'll become the tragic hero right out of your favorite stories, Hoederer!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You can't handle Theresa on your own, W.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Ines.

steps.name: W
steps.text: I'll actually bury you, you know.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph. You do you.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: She really will blow the hills apart though.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We both know she's crazy. No need to provoke her with Theresa's name.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's just pathetic, the act the she's putting on. I'd rather she knew what she wanted.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You've been in the city for so long. If she wanted to know the truth, she could've just asked you.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Did she ever ask if that Theresa was real?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She never asked me, either. She's never grown up.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She could do one of two things: Grovel at that Theresa's feet and beg for forgiveness, or plan to kill her.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But what is this that she's doing? Trying to prove that she's all great and powerful?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Or is she trying to convince herself that nothing ever happened, that all she needs to do is kill people and plant mines like she always has, and it'll all pass?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It would've been fine if she could actually stop thinking about it. But right now, she's like a little girl standing on the ice.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She takes a few steps forward, then a few steps back, looking around the same place, sinking into pointless sentimentality.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I have no idea.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Give me a break. You just don't want the extra trouble.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I didn't know you cared so much about her.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I care about me. I don't want to die because of her.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: In all seriousness, Ines, have you ever thought about going back to Kazdel?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What? Am I in the way of your great plan?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No, it's just occurred to me that W and I have a reason to stay in this war.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But what about you?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...I've got my reason too.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Here we are.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We're... inside the hill.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: They hollowed out the whole thing?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Well, that's going to make things easier for W's demolition plan.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Look at the size of these tracks, and the loading mechanism.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's a big guy.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Shh, get into the shadows.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: When's the next shift?

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Close.

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: It's always on time.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: I should've made a report to the boss. I would rather be outside, killing Victorians.

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: You're not a warrior.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: I don't need you to tell me! It's just that this place is so... oppressive.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: I see those illusions every day, the things you don't know whether they're real or not.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: It's like a maelstrom that keeps spitting out trash from another dimension.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Good thing Ulšulah is a decent woman who doesn't pick on us for no reason or abuse her authority.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Is she the youngest major ever, according to Military Commission ranks?

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: She's not a member of the Royal Court. She won't go far.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Lady Theresa and the Regent aren't blue-blood devils either.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Screw the Royal Court. Kazdel wasn't won by those old fossils huddling around in a circle.

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: But they're the strongest.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: That's because...

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: It's almost time.

steps.name: Quiet Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Go to the machine and prepare to load.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Did you hear the name they said?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Could it be...?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's not necessarily the one we're thinking of. Sarkaz names are often codenames or taken from legends.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah the Time-Stealer. Ulšulah of the Lock and Key. It's a Sarkaz legend about the Feranmut. Anyone could've drawn from it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Wait... Ulšulah the Time-Stealer?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What's the origin of your name, 'Hoederer'?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Don't have one.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Bells.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Wait, over there...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What's that?

a.text: What was that?
The hills are trembling...
No, space itself is trembling.
For an instant, I see visions beyond reckoning.
Bloated emperors crumbling in halls of gold, ancient bloodborn cutting open their wrists to feed the newborn.
Diαbolic flames burning amber. Demons with deer horns prowl beneath great bronze walls, offering battered willow wood.
The one knot falls from nothingness, splitting into countless threads; a red-skinned monster cuts off its own horn, impaling its own chest with it.
Broken shards become whole again. I see a far-away city.
Calm, peaceful, not yet wheeled, not yet drowned in hatred. Its beauty is absurd and out of place, even in a dream.
For no reason at all, I am convinced that it was Kazdel. A home that has long ceased to exist, from somewhere in history.
I want to go there, go into there. I want to see what kind of life we once led.
I lift my foot, but put it down in the same place again. I watch it quietly.
Until all is silent.
Until—
A pathetic creature that is naught but bleached bones moves slowly.
Nerve strands reach out and grab the massive containers.
It still roams this place. It is not dead yet.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This... this is the 'cargo ship'?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So big... how did Theresis...?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It... it's really...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah the Time-Stealer...
What a coincidence, right?
The legend of Ulšulah tells of Kazdel being attacked by a Feranmut that could slow the time of all things and peer into the past through the fog.
Through so many pasts the hero Ulšulah journeyed, rescuing their kin lost in the mirage of time.
Who knew that I, who took the name by happenstance, would one day witness the legend with my own eyes?
You've really ground those horns into shape, Ines. You could almost pass for a true blue Sarkaz.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Are you really going to betray General Manfred, Hoederer?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I knew you wouldn't kill Ines when I first heard the rumors, but the confidential nature of my work precluded a personal visit to Londinium to see you.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Aren't you supposed to be the handpicked successor to the Scar Market? Sounds like you're already the bone driver here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Is playing a hero of legend worth such loyalty and commitment?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Ancient things are not so appealing anymore.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Only one stuck in the past would continue to use the name.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You could give yourself a new name.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: How would old friends who came a long way to visit be able to find me then?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Care for a drink?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You didn't used to be a drinker.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Used to, huh?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You didn't used to swing your sword at me either, Ines.
